A '''lightwhip''', also known as an '''energy whip''' or a '''laser whip''', was a rare variation of the [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].

==Specifications==
{{Quote|Tell me&hellip;how does it work?''"<br />"''On the same principle as my whip&hellip;when you activate that stud on the hilt, it releases a beam of coherent energy which forms the sword blade.|Den Siva and Lumiya|<ref name="SW96">[[Star Wars (1977) 96|''Star Wars'' (1977) 96]]</ref>}}
[[File:Nightsister_JATM.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomiri]] [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] wielding a lightwhip]]

Lightwhips generally functioned on the same principles and mechanics as lightsabers, emitting a coherent beam of energy that was used as a weapon. However, rather than the straight, meter-long blades emitted by standard lightsabers, lightwhips featured long, flexible blades that often exceeded several meters in length.<ref name="JATM" /> Instead of one large crystal, they contained multiple small crystals, and the plasma in the blade had no cell barriers to keep it straight. It appeared standard for these weapons to emit only single blades, though "cat o' nine tails-style" lightwhips with multiple tassels were not unheard of, as the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lumiya]] owned one.<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref> Like [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], lightwhips came in a variety of colors and shades, including red, orange, pink, yellow, and green.

Wielded in the same manner as a conventional whip, the lightwhip was a rare and exotic weapon, an unfamiliar occurrence among traditional duelists. Due to this, lightwhip wielders enjoyed considerable leverage over opponents.<ref name="DBPoD">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> Along with its rarity, lightwhips also featured copious range, the long, flexible energy strand allowing the wielder to attack from a range of several meters.<ref name="SW96" /> The weapon was also difficult to defend against, as it could simply flex around an opponent's blade when he attempted to parry.<ref name="Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref> When multiple tassels were included, the whip was able to overwhelm the defenses of enemies by attacking them from all sides.<ref name="SW96" />

However, lightwhips featured just as many drawbacks as advantages. Unless the wielder was already a master with ordinary whips,<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> a lightwhip blade was difficult to control, able to just as easily maim an untrained wielder as an opponent, and was weaker than the standard lightsaber blade as it could not always penetrate durasteel armor or walls, and many substances could survive from a direct hit.<ref name="JATM" /> It needed to be swung wide to gain momentum for attack, and it was difficult to use defensively as flexible tassels are not well suited for parrying, leaving the wielder vulnerable to both great speed and brute force.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> In fact, lightwhip blades were even known to short out violently when struck with enough force.<ref name="SW96" />

[[File:Nightsister_Lightwhip.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Nightsister wielding a lengthy lightwhip]]

Efforts to compensate for the inherent weaknesses of lightwhips included the addition of tassels composed of solid matter, as [[Lumiya]] did with [[Lumiya's lightwhip|her weapon]].<ref name="Sacrifice" /> These variations in composition also allowed her to attack her opponent on two fronts, as the different behaviors of the energy beams and the solid strands left the weapon highly unpredictable, as well as taking advantage of flaws in Jedi training, which only prepared combatants for a weapon that was one or the other. However, this innovation was not a complete solution, as the weapon still possessed the weaknesses. Also, the inclusion of the solid strands could be countered through the use of the [[Jar'Kai/Legends|Jar'Kai dual-blade technique]], the method being to ensnare the energy strand with one blade while shredding the solid tassels with the second.<ref name="SW96" />

==History==
[[File:Githany_lightwhip.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Githany]] wielding her lightwhip against [[Kiel Charny]]]]

One of the earliest known wielders of the lightwhip was the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Githany]], who was active approximately a [[1000 BBY/Legends|millennium before the Battle of Yavin]]. According to the [[Sith Blademaster]] of the day, [[Kas'im]], she wielded the weapon not out of any advantages it presented in combat, but to exploit its rarity and unfamiliarity with most duelists. Githany wielded the weapon up until her death in the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|final battle of Ruusan]].<ref name="DBPoD" />

Lightwhip wielders active prior to and during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] include [[Ona Nobis]].<ref name="JATDH">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Deadly Hunter]]''</ref>

During their [[mission to Ord Cestus]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] fabricated a lightwhip for use by both himself and [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]]. This weapon was based on the one wielded by Ona Nobis, and first saw use during a mock duel between himself and Fisto, with Fisto masquerading as a member of [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolytes]] in order to fool the Cestus government into believing that the Separatists were interfering in their affairs. Towards the end of the same mission, Kenobi led the charge into the Cestus Cybernetics factory, wielding the lightwhip as a secondary weapon alongside his lightsaber. During the battle, the lightwhip's power cell burned out, and Kenobi discarded the weapon.<ref name="TCD">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref>

A lightwhip fell into the possession of smuggler [[Drach Coven]] and his partner, [[Mok]]. The whip was found by [[Nick Rostu]] when he was given their ship, and he later presented it to the Jedi [[Jax Pavan]]. Pavan wielded the weapon against the Falleen [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], who wielded the Jedi's own lightsaber against him.<ref name="CNJT">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> Another lightwhip wielder active at the time was the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] [[Silri]],<ref name="EaWFoC">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref> who worked for the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]].

[[File:LukeCuttingTheWhipTails.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Luke Skywalker harried by the multiple extensions of Lumiya's lightwhip]]

One of the most notable lightwhip wielders was the [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial agent]] turned [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] turned [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lady]] [[Lumiya]]. Constructing her weapon from [[Beskar/Legends|Mandalorian iron]] and utilizing a shard of the [[Kaiburr crystal]] provided by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], she also added on numerous tassels composed of leather knots studded with Mandalorian iron<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and flexible, gem speckled metal.<ref name="Tempest">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref> Created by Lumiya shortly before the close of her training under Vader,<ref name="LDSE">{{GalaxyCite|3|Lumiya: Dark Star of the Empire}}</ref> she wielded the weapon against such notables as [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]], and she used it to torture her captive on Kinooine. The weapon was ultimately lost during her final battle with Skywalker, falling into a gorge beneath them, along with her headless body.<ref name="Sacrifice" />
